Welcome {first}!
Do you have a little girl in your life who NEEDS a knitted dress?
What could be cuter than a little dress with flowers, ruffles, color and fun texture?
A fellow knitter recently challenged me to create a baby pinafore pattern. Having sons, my experience in this area is lacking, but she sent me some examples and I really got excited. (thank you, Jill!)
As I created a new Pinterest board to store all the fun examples, I found that I couldn't decide which one I liked best! So we created 2 styles in one pattern.
  • A simple 2 piece a-line style. Think of this one as a blank canvas for playing with color and adding embellishments.
  • The Empire style has a yoke and skirt. The separate pieces allow us to knit the yoke and skirt in different stitch patterns... plus opens up even more possibilities for embellishment and awesome cuteness!!!
It's your choice... make this a fast and easy project or add a bunch of color changes, lace and hand manipulation for an heirloom project.
With the included Knit it Now Dynamic pattern, you can use any machine, any yarn, any stitch pattern to reproduce something you've seen or your own design.
Scroll through our Pinterest Board below for Pinafore Inspiration.

If you want to lengthen or shorten your Pinafore:
  • A-Line: Because of the A-line shape you'll need to do a little math.
    Don't panic. We include a tool in the pattern to make it easy (see the video below)
  • Empire Style: Add or subtract rows from the skirt length

The video below walks you through using the built-in length adjustment tool. Even though the video discusses sleeves, the idea is the same. The tool will help you adjust the length of a shaped piece and re-calculate the shaping instructions for you.
The Pinafore Patterns in this course are designed with a back neck opening. But because of the size, it can be a bit of a challenge attaching a neckband to this opening on the machine.

Here's an alternative to the back neck opening. Eliminate the back neck split in the pattern and join the shoulders as shown below.
When knitting pullover sweaters for babies and kids, it's important to make sure the neck opening will fit over the head.  Looking at sizing charts, 3 month heads are 15". Neck openings are 4.5".  Yes, knitting stretches, but leaving one shoulder open is the answer for a sweater that will be worn.
Knitters have 2 choices:

  • Knit the front and back pieces as instructed
  • Join the right shoulder
  • Knit and attach the neck band per the pattern
  • On the left back shoulder pick up stitches and knit a band. Knit in ribbing and bind off or knit a doubled band, fold over and secure.
  • On the left front shoulder work the same style of band, adding buttonholes

  • Knit the front and back pieces as instructed, removing the left shoulders on waste yarn.
  • Join the right shoulder
  • re-hang the left back shoulder stitches and knit in ribbing or a doubled band
  • re-hang the left front shoulder stitches and work the same style of band, adding buttonholes
  • Pick up the neck band, including the edge of the shoulder bands and work as directed in your pattern.

There are many variables when knitting (both by hand and by machine).  
  • Different colors of the SAME yarn may knit to a different gauge
  • Different dye lots of the SAME color of the SAME yarn may knit to a different gauge
  • Different models of the SAME gauge knitting machine may knit to a different gauge.
  • The SAME size knitting needle from a different manufacturer may knit to a different gauge
  • Different people, using the exactly the SAME needles, machines, and yarns may get get different gauges
SWATCHING IS NOT OPTIONAL!
How many times have you knit something that just didn't fit?  Have you ever had colors run or fade when you washed your sweater?
So many knitting disasters can be avoided by swatching and dressing your swatch.  Machine knitters have NO EXCUSE for not swatching!  We can knit multiple swatches quickly, testing stitch patterns and tensions.  Since we don't have a lot of time invested, we can do the "throw-the-swatch-in-the-wash-with-jeans" test to see if a washable yarn will hold up.

It is important that you know how to estimate yarn for all of your knitting projects
(hint: it's based on your swatch and a little math)

components.html:
Hate math?
Try the Knit it Now tool

Instructions are for suggestions for standard gauge (mid-gauge, bulky) and for using gauge rulers.
Remember, you can knit swatches any size (as long as they are at least 5-6" square.) Be sure to be consistent and establish a template for yourself for every time you knit a swatch.

1. Cast on 60(50,30) stitches (add extra stitches so you can measure the center without edge distortion.)
  2. Knit a few rows in pattern
  3. Knit 2 rows in waste yarn (or weave a marker row)
  4. Set row counter to 000
  5. Knit the center section
    Standard gauge:
    • Knit 20 rows and knit in a yarn marker isolating the center 40 stitches
    • Knit 20 more rows and place a marker on the same needles
    • Knit 20 more rows
    Mid-Gauge:
    • Knit 10 rows and knit in a yarn marker isolating the center 30 stitches
    • Knit 10 more rows and place a marker on the same needles
    Bulky
    • Knit 15 rows and knit in a yarn marker isolating the center 40 stitches
    • Knit 15 more rows
  6. Confirm and record the total number of rows you knit for the center 60(40, 30)
  7. Knit 2 rows in waste yarn (or weave a marker row)
  8. Knit a few rows and bind off (or drop the work from the machine)
Let the swatch rest
  1. Dress the swatch as you will treat the finished item
  2. Measure the size of the 40(30, 20) stitches in the center of the swatch (between the yarn markers)
  3. Measure the size of the 60(40,30) rows between the waste yarn (or marker rows)
  4. The math
    • Divide the stitches in the middle by your measurement to get Stitches Per Inch/cm
    • Divide the rows in the middle by your measurement to get Rows Per Inch/cm
    • Multiply your stitches/rows per inch/cm times 4 to calculate stitches per 4" (10cm)
Plain or fancy, you have lots of choices with increases and decreases

Neckline shaping doesn't have to be difficult.
Practice and master shaping necklines BEFORE you start your sweater project

For fast, casual garments, rolled hems are perfect. Work a closed cast on and just start knitting! No muss or fuss! Embrace the roll!
With just a little bit of hand sewing, you can quickly add a pretty scalloped edge to your rolled edges.

This picot hem includes stitch transfers, but the effort is so worth it! The hem lays flat and is beautiful!
Use a garter bar to turn a few garter rows immediately above this hem for completely different look.
Delicate scalloped hem. 3 variations with eyelets for a beautiful beginning.

Don't let this happen to you!
Get in the habit of adding lifelines when you are knitting.
""I knit 600 rows with hand manipulation, dropped a stitch and had to rip the whole thing"
"
Instead of binding off your shoulder seams, scrap off and leave live stitches. Join the seams on the machine for a beautiful finish. (This is similar to a 3 needle bind off in hand knitting)
Careful seaming can mean the difference between "home made" and "hand made". Take time to practice different seaming techniques for your project.

Best Ever Picot Hem This is one of our favorite hems.
Basic Shaping To make seaming easier, decrease at least 2 stitches from the edge.
Lifelines Add a LIFELINE (scrap off and rehang) before starting the armhole shaping and/or before starting the neckline shaping.
Knitting each side separately, scrap off each shoulder.

components.html:
After knitting the shoulder, leave a tail at least 3x the width of the shoulder to use for this seam.

Best Shoulder Join:
  1. With right side facing, hang stitches of one shoulder from waste yarn
  2. Remove the scrap to confirm all stitches are in place (if desired)
  3. Push stitches behind the latches
  4. With wrong side facing, hang the stitches of the other shoulder in the hooks of the needles
  5. Remove the scrap if desired
  6. Carefully pull the stitches in the hooks through the first set of stitches
  7. Bind off

There are many ways to seam the side seams of your pinafore.
For a fast finish, try seaming on the machine. With a little practice, joining seams will become easy and your go-to method.

components.title: Fast finishing with seams on the machine

components.html:
For a FAST finish, work 2 rows of single crochet around the neck and armhole openings. Knit a chain loop for a button at the back neck. We chose to leave the back neck opening unfinished.
Consider a knit or crochet flower, buttons, iron-on sparkles .... you name it! What about a pocket or two?

slides.caption: Knit 4 pieces for a different style. We knit ours plain. You may choose to knit the skirt and the bodice in different stitch patterns ... or colors!
Knit the skirt sections first. We chose an easy contrasting color rolled hem.
Re-hang a skirt section over the number of needles needed for the yoke (private/wrong side facing). Gather the skirt section by evenly doubling up stitches across the row.
With the skirt stitches on the needles, follow your pattern to knit and shape the yoke
An easy rolled hem to finish the armholes.
Knit the neckband separately and join to the sweater. We chose to leave the back neck opening unfinished.

components.html:
Even with the split opening in the center back, this is a small neckline and we aren't able to pick up, attach and knit the band as you would the armholes.
Here are some tips for adding a neckband to a round neck opening, without a seam in the band.

The seam between the skirt and yoke of this dress is a perfect place to add a designer touch. We used an e-wrap cast on between the 2 pieces .
This technique is also beautiful between the neckline and neckband of a sweater. You'll probably be able to find other exciting uses!
Watch how it's done.
This technique is so useful that it's worth taking time to learn it and practice.

1. Using any swatch you have handy, e-wrap with a contrasting yarn 2 or 3 strands. Consider multi color yarn or textured yarn for interest.
  2. Rehang the edge of the swatch on some needles (you don't have to gather to get a feel for this)
  3. Close the latches and slowly and carefully knit 1 row. There is extra bulk, so make sure all the stitches knit correctly
  4. Knit a for a few inches and drop the work from the machine to admire your beautiful decorative seam!
For a different look, Try this exercise and use a chain cast on instead of e-wrap. Consider where you use this, because the seam may not have as much stretch as an e-wrap.

• 2 strands of a multi color boucle
  • Alternate knit and purl sices

  • When knitting the previous swatch, the waste yarn "ruffle" looks great!
  • What about adding a machine knit lace insert or pre-made lace yardage?
